audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Missing wet-region branch in the core model-selection lemma; Incorrect derivative in variable-angle first variation; Cosine replaces sine in refined normal boundary flux
limitations: Missing wet-region branch in the core model-selection lemma — Counterevidence: Example 1.3 explicitly supplies wet-region swapping.
Missing wet-region branch in the core model-selection lemma — Counterevidence: Page 40 restricts Sections 4-6 to an acute-angle normalization.
Missing wet-region branch in the core model-selection lemma — Counterevidence: The counterexample has a smooth interior half-plane and satisfies regularity.
Incorrect derivative in variable-angle first variation — Counterevidence: Corrected derivative retains the weighted L1 bound used by compactness and monotonicity.
Incorrect derivative in variable-angle first variation — Counterevidence: The derivative vanishes almost everywhere on the zero level set of cos(beta), so weighted definition extends.
Cosine replaces sine in refined normal boundary flux — Counterevidence: Vector identity (3.41) and tangent cone classification are consistent with the corrected coefficient.
Cosine replaces sine in refined normal boundary flux — Counterevidence: Section 3.4 expressly is not used for the main maximum-principle/Allard argument.
Negative wall mass undercounted in total-variation estimates — Counterevidence: Strict interior mass bound survives.

Negative wall mass undercounted in total-variation estimates — Counterevidence: The total-variation term in the checked trace estimates needs only a uniform dimensional bound, available from Theta+2a.
Incorrect boundary-normal Taylor coefficient — Counterevidence: Correct coefficient remains strictly negative at fixed interior angles.
Incorrect boundary-normal Taylor coefficient — Counterevidence: The homogeneous boundary Neumann condition is unchanged after correcting the coefficient.
Limits: Finite numerics corroborate proofs, not interval certificates; no author code executed.

The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.

proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:capillary. Write \(W=\{x_1=0\}\), \(S_-=\{x\in W:x_{n+1}<0\}\) and \(S_+=\{x\in W:x_{n+1}>0\}\). The manuscript permits signed varifolds \[V=V_I+\cos\beta[S]_g,\qquad V_I\ \hbox{integral in }\{x_1<0\},\] where \(g,\beta\) are \(C^1\), \(S\) is measurable, and, for compactly supported \(C^1\) vector fields tangent to \(W\), \[
 \delta_{\beta,g}V(X)
 =\int\operatorname{div}_{V,g}X\,d\mu_{V_I}
  +\int_S\operatorname{div}_{W,g}(\cos\beta X)\,d\mathcal H_g^n
 =-\int g(H^{\rm tan},X)\,d\mu_{V_I}.\] This is Definition 1.1, p. 3, and Definition 2.1, pp. 13–14. In particular, negative wall weights are expressly allowed. The model is \[P_\theta^-=\{\cos\theta\,x_1+\sin\theta\,x_{n+1}=0,\ x_1\leq0\},
 \qquad V^{(\theta)}=[P_\theta^-]+\cos\theta[S_-].\] For \(0<\theta<\pi\), \[\Theta_{V^{(\theta)}}(0,1)+(\cos\theta)^-
   =\frac{1+|\cos\theta|}{2}<1.\] Here \(a^-=\max\{-a,0\}\). This shifted signed density must not be confused with normalized total variation.

The first-variation theorem requires a strict density gap \(1-\alpha\) and small \(H^{\rm tan}\), metric error and \(D\beta\). The main graph theorem excludes the right angle and requires the origin in the interior support and closeness to a half-plane. The version based on varifold distance also requires \(C^1\) closeness of the angle, not merely small \(D\beta\). The finite-perimeter conclusion for \(S\) is used only where \(|\cos\beta|\) stays away from zero. The dense regular-set assertion and the stronger almost-everywhere assertion in Theorem 1.19 have different density hypotheses. None of these restrictions is removed in this review.

The lemma quantifies over \(\theta\) separated from \(0,\pi/2,\pi\), a \(C^1\) metric and angle, and a capillary varifold with \[0\in\operatorname{spt}V_I,\quad
 \Theta_V(0,1)+(\cos\beta(0))^-
 \leq\frac34+\frac{|\cos\theta_0|}{4},\] and arbitrarily small \(H^{\rm tan}\), metric error and \(D\beta\). It claims that small \(\operatorname{osc}_{P_\theta}(V_I,B_1)\) forces \(\mathcal D(V,V^{(\theta)})\) small and \(\beta\) close to \(\theta\), allowing addition of an integer multiple of \(\pi\).

Equation reference: eq:branch. Choose \(n=1\), \(g=g_{\rm eucl}\), \(\theta=\pi/3\), \(\theta_0=\pi/12\), \(\beta=2\pi/3\), and \[
 V=[P_{\pi/3}^-]-\tfrac12[S_+].\] Both angles are in their required ranges, \(V_I\) has multiplicity one, \(0\in\operatorname{spt}V_I\), and its oscillation relative to \(P_{\pi/3}\) is zero.

Exact counterexample. The outward conormal of the interior ray at the origin is \(\sin\theta\,e_1-\cos\theta\,e_2\). The conormal of the upper wall ray is \(-e_2\); multiplying by \(-\cos\theta\) cancels the tangential component. Thus [eq:capillary] (#eq:capillary) holds with \(H^{\rm tan}=0\). All differential smallness quantities vanish. The normalized signed density is \(1/4\), so the shifted density is \(3/4\), strictly below \(3/4+\cos(\pi/12)/4\).

Nevertheless \[V-V^{(\pi/3)}=-\tfrac12[W]\ne0.\] Consequently their distance in the manuscript’s varifold metric is a fixed positive number. Taking a constant sequence of [eq:branch] (#eq:branch) disproves (3.38) for any smaller prescribed distance tolerance and every positive smallness threshold. Moreover \[\inf_{k\in\mathbb Z}|2\pi/3+k\pi-\pi/3|=\pi/3,\] so the stated angular normalization does not rescue the conclusion. ◻

repair.content:
State convergence to either Vtheta or Vtheta-cos(theta)[wall], or impose compatible sign and normalized angle range; explicitly normalize the branch before the main proof invokes convergence.

Replace grad sin(beta) by grad cos(beta) consistently and correct the product-rule sign in Remark 3.2.

For normalized beta in (0,pi), use sin(beta) on BS and retain coefficient 1 on the free-boundary complement.

Use two copies of negative wall mass for total variation, retain one copy for mu_VI, and allow a dimensional total-mass constant.

Replace coefficient by -sin(theta)^3 and adjust angle-dependent barrier constants and displayed bounds.
